appraisal_events.evidence: "alors que tous les officiers du régiment faisaient fête à Saint-Loup, le prince de Borodino ... se borna à être obligeant pour lui dans le service ... mais il ne le reçut jamais chez lui, sauf en une circonstance particulière où il fut en quelque sorte forcé de l'inviter"; meanwhile he freely entertains "deux lieutenants roturiers".
appraisal_events.explanation: Alone among the officers, Borodino withholds from Saint-Loup the hospitality he grants commoners, classing him among "des inférieurs qui se croyaient supérieurs"; the narrator reports the withholding and its reasoning without endorsing Borodino's grounds.

appraisal_events.evidence: The narrator, seated at the captain's table, sets "la différence qu'il y avait entre les deux aristocraties": Saint-Loup's caste, having exercised no real authority for a century, treats protective affability as an aimless exercise and slaps any bourgeois on the shoulder, "le coude sur la table et le pied dans la main"; Borodino "considérait son rang comme une prérogative effective", addressing the same commoners "avec une affabilité majestueuse", and "cette bourgeoisie, il la méprisait moins".
appraisal_events.explanation: The comparison is staged to Borodino's advantage: his manner is grounded in real function and real regard, while Saint-Loup's easy familiarity is diagnosed as a caste vice that would be badly received where Borodino's family served.

appraisal_events.evidence: The lieutenant-colonel and the médecin-chef dine with him weekly and think themselves his true friends; once transferred to Beauvais he forgets them "aussi complètement ... que le théâtre de Doncières et le petit restaurant", and "à leur grande indignation" they never hear from him again.
appraisal_events.explanation: The closing anecdote shows the prince's Doncières intimacy to have been worth nothing, and the injured parties register the drop themselves.

status_effects.explanation: Saint-Loup is kept outside the captain's house — the one door in the regiment closed to him — and crosses its threshold only once, under compulsion.

The narrator's comparison lowers him: his amiability is exposed as an inherited exercise without object, and his slack bearing as something that would be ill received in the world Borodino comes from.
The same comparison credits him with an authority that still means something and with a genuine, less contemptuous bearing toward those beneath him.
Within the world of the passage his standing with the Doncières couples collapses into indignation once his abandonment of them is registered.

ambiguities: The portrait of Borodino is double-lit: the Napoleonic inheritance is at once granted real substance and mock-heroically deflated (a gaze "capable de déjouer Talleyrand" spent on trouser cloth and mess rations), so the elevation in E2 carries an ironic charge the passage never fully resolves.
